deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a category with a closed-model-like structure, with classes C (cofibrations), TC (trivial cofibrations), F (fibrations) and TF (trivial fibrations). The classes are tied by lifting properties: C = LLP(TF), TF = RLP(C), TC = LLP(F), F = RLP(TC). There is a product functor ×T (more generally ⊗T) with right adjoint Hom(T,−).

The page proves a lemma, presumably stated on the previous (blank or untranscribed) page 8:
(i) C and TC are stable under −×T,
is equivalent to
(ii) F and TF are stable under Hom(T,−).

Proof of (i)⇒(ii). Take f: X→Y in F. Then Hom(T,f) has the RLP with respect to i ∈ TC exactly when f has the RLP with respect to i×id_T. By adjunction, a lifting square for one corresponds to a lifting square for the other. Since i×T ∈ TC, f lifts against it, so Hom(T,f) ∈ F. The same argument works for f ∈ TF using stability of C under ×T.

Proof of (ii)⇒(i). For i ∈ C, i×T lies in C iff it has the LLP with respect to every f ∈ TF. By adjunction this is equivalent to i having the LLP with respect to Hom(T,f), which is in TF by assumption.

NB, generalisation. The argument is purely formal. It applies to any pair (L*, L_*) of classes determined by LLP/RLP, given an adjunction ⊗T ⊣ Hom(T,−). Grothendieck calls the hom-tensor isomorphism Hom(A⊗T,X) ≅ Hom(A,Hom(T,X)) the 'Cartan relation'. Stability of L* under ⊗T is equivalent to stability of L_* under Hom(T,−).

'Moreover': the relative (Leibniz) version. For i: A→B in L* and f: X→Y in L_*, consider the map
α(i,f): Hom(B,X) → Hom(i,f),
where Hom(i,f) denotes the fibre product Hom(A,X) ×_{Hom(A,Y)} Hom(B,Y). This is the modern pullback-hom (pullback-power).
α(i,f) has the RLP with respect to j: A'→B' iff the induced map Hom(B'⊗B, X) → Hom(j⊠i, f) is surjective. Here j⊠i is the pushout-product:
A'⊗B ∐_{A'⊗A} B'⊗A → B'⊗B.
Equivalently, j⊠i has the LLP with respect to f. So the needed condition is L*⊠L* ⊂ L*. Grothendieck remarks this holds when L* consists of monomorphisms and ⊗ is the cartesian product (in a topos or presheaf category). A marginal note says to check this 'largely more carefully; and conversely'.

Conclusion for the two pairs (C,TF) and (TC,F):
- i ∈ C, f ∈ TF ⇒ α(i,f) ∈ TF.
- i ∈ TC, f ∈ F ⇒ α(i,f) ∈ F.

These are half of the familiar SM7 / monoidal-model-category conditions. The purpose is evidently to equip the homotopy-theory framework of 'Champs' (the 1982 precursor material to Pursuing Stacks) with internal Homs that respect fibrations. For example, simplicial or cubical presheaf categories where cofibrations are monomorphisms.
errors: 'Same for f ∈ TC, using stability of C under ×T' must mean f ∈ TF. Hom(T,f) ∈ TF follows from f having the RLP with respect to C×T ⊂ C. This is a slip of the pen.

In the 'Moreover' paragraph the condition is first written as stability of L* under ?⊗T, which is equivalent to stability of L_* under Hom(T,?). But the argument that α(i,f) ∈ L_* actually needs the stronger relative condition L*⊠L* ⊂ L* (pushout-product closure). Grothendieck realises this midway: the crossed-out lines and the 'Thus we have to check' sentence show it.

The stated consequence 'i ∈ TC, f ∈ F ⇒ α(i,f) ∈ F' needs TC⊠TC ⊂ TC. It is weaker than the standard SM7 conclusion (α(i,f) ∈ TF whenever i ∈ C, f ∈ F and one of them is trivial). That conclusion would require C⊠TC ⊂ TC, which is not addressed here.

The claim 'OK if L* are monomorphisms and ⊗ = cartesian product' is right for C = monos in a topos. For TC it also needs that pushout-products of trivial cofibrations are weak equivalences, which is not argued. The margin note 'check more carefully' acknowledges this.

ideas.what: Stability of (trivial) cofibrations under −×T is equivalent to stability of (trivial) fibrations under Hom(T,−), proved by adjunction of lifting problems
ideas.modern_name: Adjunction transfers lifting properties (lemma on adjoint functors and weak factorization systems)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Quillen, Homotopical Algebra (1967); see e.g. Hovey, Model Categories (1999)
ideas.where_published: Possibly discussed in Pursuing Stacks (1983) in the context of model structures on presheaf categories

ideas.what: Tensor-hom adjunction Hom(A⊗T,X) ≅ Hom(A,Hom(T,X)), called the 'Cartan relation'
ideas.where_published: Standard throughout SGA4 and EGA (internal Hom)

ideas.what: Pullback-hom map α(i,f): Hom(B,X) → Hom(A,X)×_{Hom(A,Y)}Hom(B,Y) and its lifting properties dual to the pushout-product i'⊠i
ideas.modern_name: Leibniz construction: pushout-product / pullback-power; SM7 axiom; monoidal model category axiom
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (1967, SM7); Gabriel–Zisman (1967, pushout-products of anodyne extensions); Hovey (1999); Joyal–Tierney (2007); Riehl–Verity (Leibniz)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks may contain related remarks; not certain

ideas.what: Pushout-product of monomorphisms (with ⊗ = ×) is a monomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Monomorphisms closed under pushout-product in a topos

missed.claim: Dating evidence. The verso of the next sheet is an IBM MVS job log stamped 82160, i.e. 9 June 1982. So this stretch of the Champs notes was written after June 1982, some months before Pursuing Stacks (Feb. 1983). It shows Grothendieck already working through SM7-type 'Leibniz' lifting arguments for model structures.
missed.quote: Coming back to case of (C, TF), (TC, F), this shows that if i∈C, f∈TF, then α(i,f) is in TF
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it helps date Grothendieck's engagement with Quillen model-category technique, and his ⊠ notation for the pushout-product, before Pursuing Stacks.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but entirely standard model-category bookkeeping: adjunction of lifting properties and the pushout-product/pullback-hom (SM7). It is well established in the literature since Quillen (1967) and Gabriel–Zisman. The only mildly interesting features are the ⊠ notation for the pushout-product, anticipating modern □/Leibniz notation, and the dating to mid-1982.
transcription_corrections: 'Same for f∈TC' is as written in the image, but the intended meaning is f∈TF.
'{+in TC+}' after 'any i: A→B' in the first lines is a superscript insertion 'in TC', correct for f ∈ F.
'Hom(i,f)' throughout denotes the fibre product Hom(A,X)×_{Hom(A,Y)}Hom(B,Y), not a Hom-object of arrows.
The insertion near 'we have that' reads '(f in L_*?)'. The insertion '(L*)' above 'C' in 'j: A'→B' in C' indicates j should range over L*, not just C.
The struck-out heading '(i)(ii) ⇒ (iii)' appears twice. The original plan was a third equivalent condition (iii), replaced by the NB/Moreover remarks.
